findings.title: The D6 identity rule is private, but 421–427 are expected to group by it with no extra work
findings.description:
- D6 puts the identity rule in "a private `config_identity` in `replay/report.py`" (line 146). The key is `(model, profile, effort_sent, tool_use, max_output_tokens)`.
- Line 162 says "this slice ships no shared identity type", so later slices "apply the rule to their own record types".
- The Integration Requirement (line 186) promises that "421–427 can read a config's effort from `action_effort_sent` and group by the D6 rule, with no further effort work."

These cannot both hold. Every consuming slice would have to rebuild the five-field key, including the non-obvious `tool_use` and `max_output_tokens`, and copy those two fields onto its own config record. The slice plan entry says this slice "Provides effort-sent ... in config identity. All later slices read it", which means a reusable contract. The project's DRY rule says the same.

The lightest fix is to make the key a small public function over a `ProducerConfigRef`-shaped input, for example in `metrology/replay_models.py`, and have `replay/report.py` call it. If shared code is not wanted, the slice should drop the "no further effort work" claim. It should then say plainly that 424 and 425 must carry `tool_use` and `max_output_tokens` and rebuild the key themselves.

findings.title: Narrowing the architecture's identity rule is justified, but the architecture document still says the old thing
findings.description:
- The narrowing itself is sound. The architecture's goal at `420-arch.model-benchmark.md:40` says "config (alias, model, profile, effort sent)". D6 removes the alias from that key.
- The architecture supports this elsewhere. Line 99 says two rows only "when the effort really differed on the wire", and the slice plan's success criterion requires merging same-effort aliases.
- Adding `tool_use` and `max_output_tokens` is a necessary consequence, not scope creep. Without them, removing the alias would merge configs that send different requests.

What is missing: the slice says it "supersedes" the architecture (line 162) but never says to update the architecture document. Designers of 424 and 425 will read the old rule there. This needs a one-line edit to the architecture's Design Goals, not a design change.

findings.title: The "Components changed" list leaves out the `sq review resolve` entry point
findings.description: D3 (line 127) says `review/resolution.py` (`sq review resolve`) "resolves the same way". It also says `judge_residue_core` gains an `effort` parameter. A functional requirement (line 174) covers both entry points. But the Components changed list names only `pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/judge.py`. The task breakdown is usually built from that list, so `review/resolution.py` should be added to it.

findings.title: The findings-addressed judge's effort goes up while its spend is still not recorded
findings.description: D3 makes path 7 send the alias's effort. That can raise the judge's cost, and its spend is still missing from `pipeline.max_cost_usd` (947). The design states this, mentions it in the CHANGELOG (line 183), and files the missing usage record as a 175 issue. That is a proportionate choice. The architecture's producer-only replay strips the embedded review, so this path should not run inside benchmark runs, and the benchmark's spend-cap goal is not affected. The issue should still be filed while this slice is being built, not left for later.
